subject: Scope of variables declared in model block

messages.author: 5feb68cbfe09079c
messages.subject: Scope of variables declared in model block
parts:
Is there a technical reason why all variables declared in the model block are local?  I can't find an explanation of this limitation in the manual, which makes it seem somewhat arbitrary.  Background: I declare some transformed parameters in the model block because I don't want to have them in the output.  However, if I have to use them in the generated quantities block, I have to recompute them.

  Titus

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Scope of variables declared in model block
parts:
On Tuesday, April 28, 2015 at 1:13:42 PM UTC-7, Andrew Gelman wrote:
We have been talking about having Stan have the ability to not save all variables as output, so as not to clog up memory.  But I don’t think this has been implemented yet.
This feature would be fantastic to have.  Variable scope should not be abused to control what is going into the output.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Scope of variables declared in model block
parts:
RStan has the ability to declare which parameters, transformed parameters,
and generated quantities go into the output. CmdStan does not. I
don't know about the other interfaces.

I'm guessing you'd like to see us

* collapse the transformed parameters and model blocks into a single
block,

* allow variables declared at the top-level model block to be
in-scope in generated quantities, and

* add extra declarations (in language or out?) to control what goes
into the output.

If not, could you provide a description and an example of what scope
behavior you'd like to see?

There has to be some interplay of scope and output. For example,
it doesn't make sense to have nested local variables visible outside their
scopes, so I don't see how we could put them into the output.

There's also overhead in saving these things and passing them among
blocks --- the generated quantities have to retransform all the parameters
and reload all the transformed parameters into scope so they can be evaluated
with double values and not incur needless autodiff overhead.

- Bob

messages.author: 5feb68cbfe09079c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Scope of variables declared in model block
parts:
On 2015-04-28 Tue 22:40, Bob Carpenter wrote:
> RStan has the ability to declare which parameters, transformed parameters,
> and generated quantities go into the output. CmdStan does not. I
> don't know about the other interfaces.
>
> I'm guessing you'd like to see us
>
> * collapse the transformed parameters and model blocks into a single
> block,
>
> * allow variables declared at the top-level model block to be
> in-scope in generated quantities, and
>
> * add extra declarations (in language or out?) to control what goes
> into the output.
>
> If not, could you provide a description and an example of what scope
> behavior you'd like to see?

I don’t have a specific proposal at this point, I’m still trying to
understand how these things work in Stan (but yes, I was considering the
points you list above).

There are two separate issues: what goes into the output and what is
visible in subsequent blocks (let’s ignore variables in nested
blocks). However, there is no way to handle these issues
separately. There is only one mechanism to control both and that is
putting variables into transformed parameters. However, that is not
always desirable: I’m currently working on a model that has a loop in
the model block in which I do two things: transformation of parameters
and definition of priors for the parameters. However, I also need
access to the transformed parameters in generated quantities. To
achieve that, I have to move the transformation of the parameters to
transformed parameters. That, however, means that I need two loops
instead of one – one in transformed parameters and one in the model
block for assignment of the priors – and that makes the model
slower. The slowdown is probably also due to the overhead of passing
stuff from transformed parameters to the model block.

So it seems that I’m forced to implement the model in a less efficient
way just because transformed parameters is the only way to control the
visibility of variables. Making the transformed parameters visible also
gives me the undesired side-effect that they clutter the output where I
don’t need them.

My solution was to do the transformation in the model block for speed
and to transform the parameters a second time in generated
quantities. This is reasonably fast but makes the whole model
definition unnecessarily complex and error-prone. It’s also not quiet
as efficient as it could be because of the redundant calculations. I
don’t know how to address this but at the moment it feels like
Stan is making me jump through hoops. Could be all my fault, though,
and perhaps there is an elegant solution that I’m simply not seeing.

> There has to be some interplay of scope and output. For example,
> it doesn't make sense to have nested local variables visible outside their
> scopes, so I don't see how we could put them into the output.

Yes, I agree. My concern is only about variables declared in non-nested
blocks.

Titus

> There's also overhead in saving these things and passing them among
> blocks --- the generated quantities have to retransform all the parameters
> and reload all the transformed parameters into scope so they can be evaluated
> with double values and not incur needless autodiff overhead.
